title: The World Above
objective: Vorne holds Crestfall. Decide where you are needed.

default: It is morning in the outskirts, or the grey light that does duty for morning here.

When you wake, [missing person] is already up, sitting by what is left of last night's fire and reading their journal, the fourteen months of notes and translations. They look as though they have quite forgotten what mornings used to be for.

default.text: Maret is crouched at the edge of the clearing with a boy from the camp, who has been running most of the night. She hears him out, sends him to the fire, and comes over to you.
default.else: A boy from the Rootless camp is sitting by the fire with a blanket round his shoulders. Maret sent him, and he has been running most of the night.

default: The news is that Commander Vorne has come to Crestfall. He has brought thirty soldiers and a scholar, a woman called Seriva, and he has given notice to the town that the east road is now under the Compact. Nobody is to go east without the Compact's leave.

default.text: You knew. You read the order on the road.

text.commander:
Thirty soldiers, a headquarters in the granary, and a scholar travelling under armed escort.

Vorne has not come to look. He has come to act. The time for patience is over, and the Compact has decided it knows enough.

You remember what the soldier said in the market, that Commander Vorne was waiting until he knew enough to act. Well, now he thinks he does.
text.arcane:
Seriva. You have been thinking about her ever since [missing person] spoke of her in connection with the break in the mechanism.

A senior scholar of the Covenant travelling with the Iron Compact is an odd pairing. The two have been rivals for the wealth of this region for decades. If Seriva is working with Vorne, then either she has been doing so for a long time, or things have changed so much that old rivals have made common cause for the moment.

Or else she is not working with him at all. She is using him.
text.ranger:
Thirty soldiers on the east road means the road is shut. Anyone in the ruins who wants to go back to Crestfall will have to explain themselves to the Compact, and that means you.

You begin to think of other ways out of the ruins that keep clear of the road altogether.
text.cipher:
The notice is cleverer than it looks. Vorne isn't worried about who goes east. He wants to control what comes back: news, and things, and people.

He means to be the first to know what is in the ruins. The notice has nothing to do with keeping anyone safe. It is to make sure nobody knows anything he doesn't.

choices.text: Go back to Crestfall. Things have changed, and you need to see for yourself.

text: [missing person] looks at you when you say it. They do not object, quite. It is more complicated than that.
"If you go back," they say, "and the Compact shuts the road properly, you may not be able to come back."
They are quiet a moment. "Then go," they say. "And come back. I will be here."
They say it quite simply. They have had fourteen months of practice at waiting. You leave the outskirts and go west.

text.text: Maret picks up her pack without being asked. "I am coming," she says. "My people are under that notice."

choices.text: Send Maret back to Crestfall with the news, and stay in the ruins.

default.text:
Maret has been thinking the same thing. "Somebody needs to know what is in here," she says. "And somebody needs to know what Vorne is doing." She looks at [missing person], the first long look between them since you found them, and something passes between the two of them that you can't make out. "I will go back and keep the camp safe. I will send word if Vorne moves on the road."

She goes. You watch her through the outskirts until the ordinary forest hides her.

choices.text: Stay in the ruins. The ritual comes first.

default.text:
You decide that the ritual is what matters, and the rest is only the circumstances. Vorne's coming makes it more urgent, but it doesn't change what comes first.

"How long do we need?" you ask [missing person].

"To prepare you properly? Three days at the least. Five would be better." They look towards Crestfall, which you cannot see through the trees, though you know it is there. "We have days. We do not have weeks."

"Then we start today," you say.

text.default:
The outskirts are quieter now. The last sounds of the ordinary world, a cart a long way off and a bird that has not yet learned to keep away from the forest, die away as the morning settles.

[missing person] sits across from you with their journal open on their knees. They have been getting ready for this for fourteen months. You can see it in the way they sit, like somebody who has rehearsed a thing so often that the rehearsing has worn right through.

"I need to explain what this is," they say. "Not how it works. What it is. If you understand what you are agreeing to, everything else follows."

They begin.

choices.text: Go on.

text.default:
The mechanism was not built to hold the curse in, they tell you. It was built to finish something, to close a circle that was left open by people who meant to come back and never did. The curse is the unfinished work leaking out through the gap. The ritual does not destroy the curse. It finishes what was begun, and closes the gap from the inside.

"So whoever does it has to go inside," you say.

"Yes," they say. "And come out again. That part is not certain."
text.commander:
You listen with the part of you that weighs up a position and the part that doesn't, and both are paying close attention.

"What decides whether we come out?"

They look at their notes. "The mechanism reads whether the two people understand what they are finishing. It does not read it as a scholar would. It reads it as a lock reads a key. The shape must fit. If we are in the chamber and it reads us and finds us wanting, if we are not the right two, it will keep us." They pause. "It will not be unkind about it. But it will keep us."

You take that in. The danger is real. The job is still the job.
text.arcane:
The mechanism reading the two people. You have been turning it over ever since [missing person] first described the ritual.

"What exactly does it read?" you ask. "What makes a fit?"

They spend twenty minutes trying to put the old text into words that keep its sense. When they have finished, you understand that the mechanism reads something like this: how much two people mean to each other, weighed against how much brought them here. It is a kind of proportion, or a kind of chord.

"The first two who did it were bonded," they say. "And they chose to finish the work because it mattered more to them than anything else they might have done. Both must be true."
text.ranger:
You are thinking about the chamber as a place: what is in it and what isn't, and how you would get out of it.

"How long do we have to be in there?"

"The text says until the mechanism has finished reading us. An hour at the least. Perhaps longer, as worn as it is now." They pause. "From outside there is no way of telling when it has finished. You will know from inside. The text says you cannot mistake it. It feels like something settling that has been unsettled a very long time."

Nothing will show on the outside. Pol, waiting there, will have to trust you to know when it is done.
text.cipher:
You are listening for what [missing person] isn't saying.

"There's a danger you haven't mentioned," you say.

They pause. "Yes."

"Suppose the mechanism reads us and decides we're not enough. Not that we're the wrong people, but that what's between us isn't enough. What happens then?"

They look at their hands. "The text is not clear about it. I think on purpose. The people who wrote it did not want to put anyone off trying." They look up. "I have thought about it for fourteen months. The best I can make of it is that the mechanism closes anyway, with us inside it." They pause. "For good."

choices.text: "Tell me all of it. We have time today."

default.text:
They teach you all morning and well into the afternoon.

It is not the words of the ritual yet. Those come later, when you are ready to hold them. Today is the groundwork: what the mechanism is, how it reads people, what the chamber will feel like, and what you will need to stay awake to when the reading begins. They try to tell you what it will be like to be seen completely, by something that has been waiting for exactly this.

At one point they stop and look at you as though asking something without asking it.

"I'm still here," you say.

They seem to settle. "I know," they say. "I only needed to see it."

They go on teaching. Outside, the forest is very quiet. So far the curse has not got into this clearing to any extent you can measure. You have a few days, and you mean to use them.

choices.text: "What does this cost you? Not in principle. You, yourself."

success.text:
They are quiet a long while.

"Fourteen months," they say at last. "I have been in this forest fourteen months, waiting for the one person who could finish it with me. I was not alone, exactly. But I was alone in that way." They pause. "The ritual is not what costs me. The fourteen months were the cost. The ritual is what they were for."

You look at them. If you know what to look for, you can see the fourteen months of waiting in them. They have carried it so long they have forgotten how to put it down.

"Then let's not waste what you paid," you say.

They nod, and take up the lesson again, and this time they sit a little differently, as though they had put something down.

success_at_cost.text:
"Fourteen months of..." they begin, and stop.

They look at the fire for a while. "Ask me again when it is done," they say.

Then they take up the lesson where they left off, and you let them.

failure.text:
They turn the question aside, easily, as people do who have been turning it aside from themselves for fourteen months.

"It is nothing I cannot manage," they say. "Let us go on."

You let it go. There will be time for that later, or there won't, and then it won't matter.

They go on with the lesson.

default: The Compact checkpoint is two miles east of Crestfall, where the cobbles begin. There is a barricade of timber, two soldiers, and a small fire.

default.text: You stayed in the ruins a day longer than was wise. The barricade is taller than the boy described.

default: They see you before you see them, so they have been watching. When you are near enough to speak, one of them steps forward like a man following his orders to the letter.
"East road's under Compact jurisdiction, [sir/ma'am]," he says. "Name, where you've come from, and your business on the road."

default.text: "Cael's asking about a packet," the other soldier says, to nobody in particular.

text.commander:
You weigh up the checkpoint in the first few seconds. There are two soldiers in sight and probably two more within call. The barricade is solid, but it is not meant to stay. It was built to be moved, which means it was built to let the right people through.

You give your name. You tell them where you have been and why, truthfully, though not completely. The soldier writes it down.
text.arcane:
Somebody chose this spot. It is not the easiest place on the road to defend. It is the place that can be seen from furthest off in both directions.

The checkpoint is not there to keep anyone out. It is there to be seen.
text.ranger:
You walk up to the checkpoint at a pace that says you know they are there, you are not trying to avoid them, and you have nothing to hide. It is not a pace that comes naturally to you, and you have to think about it.

The soldier steps forward. The other one has his hand near his sword, but easily. They are not looking for trouble.
text.cipher:
You had a minute to get your story ready before you reached them, and it is ready. Every part of it is true, and the parts are in the order most likely to get you what you want.

The soldier asks your name, where you have come from and your business. You give him all three.

choices.text: Give your name and say you've been looking round east of the town, and are on your way back.

bonus.label: The Compact does not trust you
Cael is still waiting for his packet

success.text:
The soldier writes it down. He asks whether you saw anything worth reporting. You tell him about the east road, the empty village of Harrow, and the edge of the forest. You say nothing about the ruins, or the inner approach, or what you found at the end of it.

He nods. "Lieutenant Cael wants a word with anyone coming back from beyond Harrow," he says. "When you're settled, you'll find him at the Compact post in town."

He stands aside and you walk through.

success_at_cost.text:
The soldier takes your story, but then he asks you something you weren't expecting: whether you met anyone else beyond Harrow. You manage it. You don't think he believed everything you said, and you don't think he disbelieved it either.

You walk through. Cael will want to speak to you.

failure.text:
He keeps you at the checkpoint for the best part of an hour. There are more questions, and a second soldier is called over, and in the end a note is written and sent off towards the town.

You are not held. But as you walk through you know that your story has been written down for somebody to look into.

choices.text: Leave the road and go round through the trees.

success.text: A hundred yards short of the barricade you step off the road into the alders and keep low. The soldiers are watching the road, and nobody is watching the ditch. You come out on the cobbles behind them, muddy to the knee, with your name in nobody's book.

success_at_cost.text: You get round, though not cleanly. A branch cracks, and one of the soldiers turns and stares into the trees. You wait in the wet until he looks away again. By the time you reach the cobbles the light is going.

failure.text: You are halfway round when a voice says, "That's far enough." A third soldier has been sitting in the trees all along. He walks you back to the barricade and writes your name down slowly, so that you can watch him do it.

choices.text: Leave the road a mile early and come in through the alder brake.

default.text: A mile short of the barricade you step off the cobbles into the alders, and come into Crestfall as the deer used to, along the ditch behind the tannery. Nobody sees you, and nobody writes anything down.

choices.text: Mention that you've been working with Cael.

default.text:
At Cael's name the soldier's manner changes at once. He doesn't quite unbend, but very nearly.

"Cael said to expect you," he says, so Cael has been preparing for your return. "He wants to see you as soon as you're in. The Compact post, north side of town."

choices.text: Walk up to the barricade. They know you.
choices.locked_hint: Needs the Compact to know you

default.text: The soldier looks at you, and then at his book, and lifts the bar. "Lieutenant Cael said you might come back this way," he says. He doesn't write anything down.

choices.text: Put ten coins on the barricade.

default.text: He looks at the coins a while. Then he sweeps them into his hand and lifts the bar. "Didn't see you," he says. The other one looks at the fire.

default: Crestfall has changed in the few days you were away. It isn't a dramatic change, but you can see it, as you can see a house has changed hands.

Thirty Compact soldiers are quartered on the town, and go about it like men who have done this in other towns before. They aren't rough. They are orderly. They have taken over three buildings, posted up timetables, and set up a place by the old fountain in the market to hand out supplies.
The town has taken it as small frightened towns always take orderly authority, with relief and resentment together, and has not yet decided which is the stronger.
The curse is worse. You feel it the moment you come into the town. It presses harder than when you left, and everything is greyer. However fast the mechanism is wearing, it has not slowed down.

default.text: Tonight there is a second still figure in the square, an old man by the dry fountain. Nobody has moved him.
Two stalls are open. The rest are bare frames, and nobody has taken the frames down.

text.commander:
Thirty soldiers will change any town. The balance has shifted. The Covenant is much less in evidence; its shrine is still open, but the streets are no longer theirs. The Rootless camp outside the town is still there, according to the soldier at the checkpoint, for now.

Vorne has not moved against the camp yet. That tells you something about him, either that he can hold back or that he has other things on his mind.
text.arcane:
You feel Seriva before you see her. That is not quite true, of course, but you can see what she has done to the way the town talks. People say less. Things that were talked about freely three days ago are now spoken of in lower voices, if they are spoken of at all.

Somebody is deciding what people may say, and to whom. It is Seriva's doing, or the doing of somebody who takes her orders.
text.ranger:
There are fewer animals than when you left. The cat under the north porch has gone. You look for tracks and find nothing recent.

You read it as you read the weather from the birds. When the animals go, the storm is already on its way.
text.cipher:
You redraw your picture of Crestfall as you walk. There are Compact soldiers in seven places you can see, and the Covenant has drawn back. There are three new faces, not soldiers, but with the Compact, scholars or clerks most likely.

And there is one face you don't know but mark down at once as important: a woman in her sixties going through the market as though she knows where everything is, though she is supposed to have arrived only three days ago.

choices.text: Go to the Tallow, and get the news from Aldous.

default.text:
Aldous is behind his bar when you come in, which is where Aldous always is. He looks up, and you see him ease. He had given you up.

"You came back," he says.

"I said I would."

He pours you something without being asked. "Strange few days," he says.

choices.text: Go to the Rootless camp and see how Maret and the camp are faring.

text: The camp is still there. You had not been sure it would be. Maret has got there before you. Branch is at the edge of it, watching the town. He has been watching it for some time, and he does not like what he sees.

choices.text: Find the woman you took for Seriva, and begin there.

success.text:
You find her at the Covenant shrine, which she seems to be using as her headquarters, much to Edric's evident discomfort. She is studying a map when you come in, an old and detailed map of the country east of Crestfall.

She looks up as you enter and takes your measure in about three seconds. She is thorough, and practised, and good at it.

success_at_cost.text: You find her at the shrine. She sees you come in; she was already watching the door. You are reading her while she reads you, and she is better at it.

failure.text: You go looking for her, and she finds you. She has been watching you since you came through the gate. She comes up to you in the market square without any hurry, having already decided how this is going to go.

choices.text: Find Sen at the docks.

default.text: The docks are empty except for one figure at the end of the pier.

choices.text: Report to Cael.

default.text:
Cael is at the granary door. He listens to as much as you choose to tell him, and pays you the forty without counting it twice.

"The Commander will want to hear this himself," he says. "He likes to know who has been where."

text.default:
Sen is at the end of the pier with a line in the water and no bait on it. He doesn't look round.

"Thought you'd come," he says. "Or hoped. One of the two."

You sit down on the edge beside him. The river goes by, black and slow.

"Three weeks before you came," he says. "Bit more. There was a boat. Covered over, no lamp. It didn't come in to the docks, it put in up there by the old willows." He nods upstream without taking his eyes off the water. "One person got off. A woman, grey coat. She stood on the bank and looked at the town like she was counting it."

He winds in his line.

"I saw her in the square yesterday, with Vorne's lot. Walking about like she'd only just got here."

choices.text: Thank him, and go and find Aldous.

default.text: "Don't thank me," he says. "I didn't do anything. That's the trouble with this town."

choices.text: "Why didn't you tell anyone?"

default.text: "Who'd I tell?" He looks at the water. "Cael? He'd write it down. Edric? He'd pray about it." He casts the empty line again. "You're the first one who's come back. I thought I'd wait for someone who came back."

default: Aldous tells you what he has seen in three days, as exactly as a man who has been keeping careful accounts in his head.

Vorne arrived with thirty soldiers and the Covenant woman, Seriva, who came as what he called an adviser. The Compact took three buildings without asking anybody, and put up the notice about the east road within six hours of arriving.
Seriva has been to the shrine twice. Both times she and Edric had a conversation that Edric plainly did not enjoy.

default.text: Wren, the still man who used to sit by the fire, has gone. He walked east two days ago, the morning after Vorne came, as if all the commotion had stirred something in him and pointed him at the forest. Nobody tried to stop him. Nobody knew what to do.
default.else: The still man by the fire has gone. You never learned his name, and Aldous tells it you now: Wren. He walked east two days ago, the morning after Vorne came, as if all the commotion had stirred something in him and pointed him at the forest. Nobody tried to stop him. Nobody knew what to do.

default: "How many others?" you ask.
Aldous puts down his cloth. "Since you left? Six. All east."

default.text: He pours you a drink you didn't ask for. When you point at it he looks at the glass for a while, as though it belonged to somebody else.

text.commander:
Six people in five days. It is getting worse faster than [missing person] said it would.

Either the mechanism is wearing out quicker than they reckoned, or the Compact's coming has made things worse: a great many people crowded into a small place, the strain of being occupied, or something Seriva brought with her.
text.arcane:
Six people in five days. The mechanism is going faster. What you were told in the chamber was too hopeful.

You wonder what Seriva's being here might mean for the mechanism. If she was the one who broke it twenty years ago, if she worked something on it at the moment she broke it, then her being near Ashenveld again might be stirring up whatever she did then.
text.ranger:
Six people walking east, and each of them a family and a past and a future, going where nobody can follow.

Wren was the first. You knew Wren, only a little and not well, but enough to know he was a decent man with a wife who loved him and a farm he cared about. Whatever lies beyond the marker line has Wren now.
text.cipher:
Six people. Aldous has been counting them carefully. He is frightened, and counting is what he does about it.

"Seriva," you say. "What's she actually doing here? Not as the Covenant's adviser. What is she really doing?"

Aldous looks at you. "I don't know," he says. "But she asked Edric to show her the Covenant's papers on Ashenveld, the last twenty years of them. He showed her what he had. She spent six hours reading them, and when she'd done, she burned the copies."

choices.text: "What about the Rootless camp? Has Vorne moved against it?"

default.text:
"Not yet," Aldous says. "But..." He stops. "There's a girl at the camp. Young. She came three days ago, the night before Vorne rode in. She's..." He hesitates. "She's showing the first signs. The dimming. And she's Vorne's daughter."

You take that in.

"Does he know she's there?"

"I don't know what he knows," Aldous says. "I know if he finds out, the camp's in trouble. Either he tries to take her back, and Maret won't stand for it, or he tries to break the camp up because his daughter went to them and not to him."

choices.text: "Tell me everything you've noticed about Seriva."

success.text:
Aldous tells you, with an innkeeper's eye for detail: how she moves about rooms as though she had been in them before, the questions she asked Edric, the way she looked at the east road when she thought nobody was watching.

"She isn't advising Vorne," Aldous says. "She's running him. He asks her where to put his soldiers and she tells him. He's the one with the authority, and she's the one who knows things, and the two of them together are something I haven't got a word for."

He pauses. "She's been in Ashenveld before. I'd bet everything I own on it."

success_at_cost.text: Aldous tells you what he has. She is running Vorne, not advising him, and he thinks she has been in Ashenveld before.

failure.text: Aldous tells you what he has seen, but he can't tell you what it means. He notices a great deal, but he is not a schemer. You will have to work it out for yourself.

default: The Rootless camp is tense, as a place is when it has been threatened without anybody quite saying so.

Branch is at the edge of the camp. Lira is in the middle of it with two others the curse has partly taken, keeping up the routine Maret has set for them. And in a corner of the camp, in a tent made as comfortable as any tent here can be, there is a girl of about seventeen with grey at her fingertips and the faraway look of the first stages of the curse.
This is Issa Vorne, the Commander's daughter.
She doesn't know who you are. She looks at you as you come over with the loose attention of the early stages, neither gone nor quite there.
The herb garden has begun to go yellow along one edge. Branch has noticed. He has put a row of stones along it, as though that might help.

default.text: Maret says, without looking up, "You were right to send me back. I have not forgiven you for it."

text.commander:
You look Issa over with a trained eye. It is early, the fingertips and the faraway look. She may not be past helping. Maret's ways have slowed it in others at this stage.

But Issa Vorne at the Rootless camp is a very serious problem. If Vorne knows she is here, it will decide everything he does next. If he doesn't know, somebody will tell him soon.
text.arcane:
You can read the curse on Issa clearly. It is recent, no more than a fortnight. It is still thin enough that something might be done to slow it.

What matters is whether Commander Vorne knows the Rootless camp is the safest place for his daughter just now, and whether knowing it would change how he treats the camp.
text.ranger:
The way Issa looks at you is not the emptiness you have seen in the others. It is distance. She is still in there, further back than she ought to be at her age and at this stage, but she is there.

"You came from the east," she says. Somehow she can tell.
text.cipher:
Issa Vorne is the most important person in the Rootless camp. She is the daughter of the man who commands every soldier in the region, she is afflicted, and she is in the camp of people her father has not yet moved against.

She is an opportunity, and a danger, and a frightened, ill girl who has come somewhere that felt safe. You try to keep all three in mind at once.

choices.text: Talk to Issa. Find out what she knows, and how she came here.

success.text:
She talks to you slowly, putting each sentence together before she says it.

She came to the camp because she knew about it. She had met Lira in the town once, before Lira went to the camp, while Lira was still well enough to talk in the market, and Lira told her about it. When the curse touched her, she knew where to go.

"My father," she says, and stops. "He'll fix it. That's what he does." There is a pause, and a good deal in it. "Or he'll fix it in a way that makes it worse. He does that too."

And then, carefully: "I found something. In the outskirts of the ruins, the day before it started. I've got it here."

She brings out a piece of stone. Its surface has been worked and carved, and you know the look of it. It is a piece of the sealing mechanism.

success_at_cost.text: She tells you a little. She came because she knew about the camp. She found something in the outskirts of the ruins and has it with her. She shows you the piece of stone, but she won't say how she found it, or what she was doing in the outskirts.

failure.text:
She doesn't answer you in any way that makes sense. It is a bad day for her; she is further off than she was yesterday. Maret says to try again tomorrow.

But you see the piece of stone in her hand, and the way she holds on to it.

choices.text: Talk to Branch, and get his view of how safe the camp is.

default.text:
Branch gives you his view without any preamble.

"Vorne has not moved on the camp because he does not know his daughter is here," he says. "When he finds out, and he will, somebody will tell him, he can do one of three things. He can take her by force, which means fighting us. He can ask us to give her up, which gives Maret something to bargain with. Or he can leave her here, which means admitting the camp is the best place for her. He will not do that."

He looks round the camp. "We have perhaps three days before someone talks. Perhaps less."

text.default:
Pol, the camp's healer, is in the herb garden. She is seventy, and has said perhaps ten words to you so far. She works with great attention, as she does everything. It is not that she has stopped noticing things. She keeps her noticing for exactly where it is wanted.

She looks up as you come over, and looks at you as she looks at a plant to see whether it is healthy, thoroughly and without any fuss.

"You were in the ruins," she says.

"Yes."

"You found the one you were looking for."

"Yes."

She is quiet a moment. "They found the sealing text."

You stop. She knew it before you told her, which means she knew it was possible, which means she knows about the text.
text.commander:
"You left the Covenant because of what you read in the archives," you say.

"Yes," she says.

"The whole sealing text."

"Yes."

You look at her: seventy years old, with her herb garden, three years at the camp and fifteen since she left the Covenant. It all adds up to a woman who has been waiting in one place for something to become possible.

"You've been getting ready," you say.
text.arcane:
You sit down across from her in the herb garden and say nothing for a moment. You both know this is not going to be a casual conversation.

"The text needs two people," you say.

"Yes," she says.

"Two who are bonded."

"The word means more than that," she says. "In the old language it means people who lived through the same things while they were still being made, and made each other. The mechanism reads what is between them, not only what they want."

You think about it. "Then that's why they chose me."

"Yes," says Pol. "For exactly the reason the text gives."
text.ranger:
You sit down across from Pol and let her take the conversation at her own pace, which turns out to be brisk.

"The sealing text," she says, "needs two people and one thing more. Something that was part of the old mechanism. A piece of it, that still remembers what it was for."

You think of Issa and the piece of stone.

"The piece Issa found," you say.

Pol nods. "I have been looking for it for three years."
text.cipher:
Pol sees you reading her, and decides to give you what she has all at once rather than a bit at a time.

"I left the Covenant because the whole sealing text tells you what the ritual costs," she says. "Not what it costs the two people. What it costs the Covenant. The purification the Covenant means to do is not the sealing ritual. It is another ritual. It uses the same mechanism, but it does something else."

She looks at you steadily. "The Covenant's ritual seals the mechanism by destroying everything the power has touched. The old ritual seals it by giving the power back what it was made for." She pauses. "They are not trying to seal the curse. They are trying to be rid of it by being rid of everyone it has touched. That is a very great difference."

choices.text: "What do you need? What will it take to do the real ritual?"

default.text:
Pol counts on her fingers.

"The two people, bonded as the text says. Your person and you, or any other two who fit."

"The piece of the mechanism that Issa found. The ritual needs something that still belongs to the mechanism as it was."

"Time. It cannot be hurried. The text says the two must stay in the chamber long enough for the mechanism to read them through. An hour at the least."

She looks at you. "And one thing more. Somebody outside the chamber who understands what is happening, and can act if it goes wrong. A witness." She looks at her hands. "I have been waiting fifteen years to be that witness."

choices.text: "Tell me about Seriva. You were both in the Covenant archives."

success.text:
Pol is quiet for a moment.

"Seriva was the best archivist the Covenant had in a generation," she says. "She understood the old texts better than most scholars ever do." She pauses. "Twenty years ago she proposed an experiment. She wanted to find out whether the mechanism could be altered, made stronger and more complete, so that it sealed more."

"And the Covenant agreed."

"Yes," says Pol. "I voted against it, and I was overruled." She looks at the garden. "What she did to the mechanism, the change she tried to make, unsettled it. The seal began to fail at once. She has spent twenty years trying to mend it with a different ritual, one that would never require her to admit that the damage was hers."

success_at_cost.text: Pol tells you that Seriva was at the mechanism twenty years ago, and that something she did there unsettled it. What exactly she did, and why, Pol is not willing to say in full.

failure.text: "Ask Seriva," says Pol. "She will not tell you the truth. But the way she avoids it will tell you something."

default: Seriva is at the shrine when you find her, or she lets herself be found there, which comes to the same thing.

She is in her sixties, small and solid, used to rooms where people defer to her, and long past needing them to. She looks at you as you come in like a woman finishing an assessment she began the day you arrived in Crestfall.
Edric is in the room. He stood up when Seriva sat down, and he has stayed standing.

default.text: Her eyes go to the cord round your neck. "Edric gave you one of mine," she says. "I made those. Twenty years ago."

default: "You went east," she says, "and you came back. Most people who go east do not come back." She pauses. "So either you are exceptionally capable, or exceptionally lucky, or you found what you were looking for and it was not in the deepest part of the ruins."
She waits to see which of these you will admit to.
text.commander:
You give her nothing she is looking for, and everything you do say is true.

"I went to Harrow," you say. "Had a look at the edge of the forest. Came back."

She looks at you. She doesn't believe that is all of it, and she can't prove that it isn't.

"Harrow is interesting," she says. "What did you find there?"
text.arcane:
You look at her, and she looks at you, and you both understand that this is a conversation between two people who know more than they mean to say, and are each trying to find out how much the other knows.

"You've been in Ashenveld before," you say.

"Twenty years ago," she says at once, owning it before you can spring it on her. "I was doing research on the Covenant's behalf."

"On the ruins."

"On the region," she says, and the difference is quite deliberate.
text.ranger:
Half a minute is enough to tell you what she is. She has known about Ashenveld and the ruins for twenty years, and for twenty years she has kept that knowledge on a short leash, letting out only what suited her.

"You know what's in the ruins," you say.

"I know what was in the ruins twenty years ago," she says. "Things change."
text.cipher:
She is very good. She is doing to you exactly what you are doing to her, and she has been doing it longer.

"You're here because the seal failed," you say. "And you're here because you know why it failed."

She pauses. "Everyone knows the seal has been failing," she says.

"Not everyone," you say. "You, in particular."

The pause before she answers tells you that you are right.

choices.text: "You broke the mechanism twenty years ago. You're here to mend what you did."

success.text:
She looks at you a long while.

Then she sits down. You have not seen her sit before; she has been standing since you came in.

"Yes," she says, quietly and completely. "I broke it. It was not carelessness. I believed what I was doing would make it stronger, and I was wrong." She looks at her hands. "I have spent twenty years trying to repair what I did. The Covenant's purification will work. It is not the old ritual; it is another way of going about the same problem. But it will stop the curse."

"At what cost?" you ask.

"At whatever cost the situation requires," she says, and now she sounds like herself again. The admission is over and the control has come back. But she did admit it, and you have it.

success_at_cost.text:
She does not say yes. But she does not deny it as she would deny something untrue. She steers away from it: what matters is the cure, not the cause. The purification will stop the spread, and the cost is acceptable.

She didn't deny it, and that is as good as a yes.

failure.text:
She turns it aside easily. She has been turning aside this accusation, or the fear of it, for twenty years. You have pushed too hard, and she has shut.

"The Covenant's ritual is the proper answer to the present situation," she says. "I am here to see that it is performed correctly, and soon."

choices.text: Ask her for the number for Crestfall, out loud, so Edric hears it.

default.text:
"How many," you ask, "in Crestfall?"

Seriva glances at Edric before she answers, which is the first unguarded thing you have seen her do. "At the present rate," she says, "a fifth."

Edric has known the doctrine for thirty years and preached it from the pulpit. You watch him hear the number for his own town, for the first time. He sits down.

choices.text: "You've been here three weeks longer than Vorne. Why?"

default.text:
She doesn't ask how you know.

"I wished to see the threshold for myself before anyone arrived to argue about it," she says. "I had been there before, a long time ago. I needed to know how far it had come." She folds her hands. "That is all I will say about it in this room."

It is quite enough to tell you the rest.

choices.text: "What does the purification cost? Who pays for it?"

success.text:
She is quiet a moment. Then she answers, and you can tell she has had the answer ready for years.

"The purification seals the mechanism by removing everything the power has changed far enough. People, animals, buildings. The further the change has gone, the more completely the ritual removes it." She pauses. "In Crestfall, at the present rate of spread, it would affect perhaps a fifth of the people. In the villages to the east, in Harrow, there would be nobody left at all."

She looks you in the eye. "That is why it must be done before a fifth becomes a third, and a third becomes a half."

success_at_cost.text: She tells you the cost in terms that are perfectly accurate and leave all the feeling out. People far gone in the curse would not survive the ritual. How many there would be depends on how far it has spread.

failure.text: She gives you the doctrine: the purification is necessary, the cost will be in proportion to the need, and the Covenant knows how to do it with as little harm as possible. You don't believe the last part, and you can't prove it.

choices.text: Tell her what she is afraid you found.

default.text:
"You were in the chamber twenty years ago," you say. "The break is yours."

She doesn't move, and that is your answer. People who are surprised move.

"You have been very busy," she says.
